items.title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation systems face a context problem where undisciplined loops lead to the inclusion of unused information. Knowledge compilation, an ingestion pipeline enriching documents with structures like entity graphs and ontologies, is proposed as the missing layer. This compilation serves as a supply layer rather than a better retriever, as structural artifacts do not inherently boost retrieval accuracy. A navigation tree based on claim-evidence pairs can significantly reduce query tokens, offering efficiency gains. The proposed RAGFlow pipeline creates an agent-native database of compiled, governed context for improved system performance.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses" details a method for improving retrieval in agentic systems through knowledge compilation. This research proposes a knowledge compilation layer to address the context problem in retrieval-augmented generation systems by enriching documents with structures like entity graphs and ontologies. The methodology involves creating an ingestion pipeline that compiles knowledge into structured artifacts, establishing a supply layer rather than directly improving retrieval accuracy. A navigation tree based on claim-evidence pairs is introduced to reduce query tokens, resulting in efficiency gains. The proposed RAGFlow pipeline constructs an agent-native database of compiled and governed context to enhance overall system performance. This work suggests that structuring knowledge can provide a foundation for more effective agentic reasoning systems.

items.title: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
items.summary: Web agents are vulnerable to adversarial content injection on websites, which existing evaluations fail to capture by only assessing text-level attacks. The research introduces REEF, a benchmark of executable environments with verification to measure web agent security vulnerabilities. ANGLER is an adaptive framework that uses execution feedback from verifiers to guide LLM-based mutation for red-teaming. ANGLER achieved an end-to-end attack success rate of 20.36% against eight VLM-based agents. Attacks generated by ANGLER significantly reduce the success rate of benign tasks, dropping it from 61.9% to 44.4%.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents" details a method for evaluating and attacking web agents by introducing a benchmark and an adaptive attack framework. The research established REEF, a benchmark of executable environments with verification, and introduced ANGLER, an adaptive framework that uses execution feedback to guide large language model mutation for red-teaming. This process involves using execution feedback from verifiers to guide LLM-based mutation for adversarial generation. The ANGLER framework achieved an end-to-end attack success rate of twenty point three six percent against eight vision-language model based agents. Attacks generated by ANGLER demonstrated a significant reduction in success rates for benign tasks, decreasing the success rate from sixty one point nine percent to forty four point four percent. This work indicates a need for more comprehensive security evaluations of web agent systems.

items.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC) is a training-free method that compresses context in long-horizon LLM agents using soft tokens instead of hard tokens. ASTC utilizes the model's recurrent dynamics and hybrid GDN-attention to capture absorbed information. This approach allows the system to carry context forward as agentic soft tokens while preserving exact values as hard tokens. Experiments show ASTC achieves accuracy matching or exceeding uncompressed agents with fewer Attention Pairs. This method demonstrates a model-native way to manage evolving task representations efficiently.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" details a training-free method for compressing context in long-horizon large language model agents using soft tokens. The research introduces Agentic Soft-Token Compression or ASTC, a technique that leverages the model's recurrent dynamics and hybrid gradient dynamics networks to capture absorbed information. This method utilizes soft tokens to carry context forward while retaining exact values as hard tokens. Experiments indicate that ASTC achieves accuracy comparable to or superior to uncompressed agents while requiring fewer attention pairs. This approach provides a model-native mechanism for efficiently managing evolving task representations within complex agentic systems. The findings suggest a path toward more efficient and scalable context management for advanced language model agents.

items.title: ART of PIV: Agentic Real-Time Particle Image Velocimetry for Active Flow Control
items.summary: Particle image velocimetry (PIV) accuracy is hindered by subjective choices in the estimation pipeline, especially when used for real-time flow control. ART of PIV introduces an agent that automates pipeline configuration selection for each image pair based on a measurement objective. This learned agent reduces end-point error in various estimators by 12.2-22.4% compared to single estimators at matched speeds. In a simulated task, ART of PIV reduced the mean normalized closed-loop cost by 13.24-13.59 percentage points. Experimental results show ART of PIV effectively controls flow in physical systems, such as tracking prescribed flow fields.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "ART of PIV: Agentic Real-Time Particle Image Velocimetry for Active Flow Control" details a method for improving the accuracy of particle image velocimetry in real-time flow control. The research introduces an agent designed to automate the selection of pipeline configurations for each image pair based on a specific measurement objective. This learned agent demonstrated a reduction in end-point error in various estimators ranging from twelve point two to twenty-four percent when compared to single estimators operating at matched speeds. In a simulated task, the method achieved a reduction in the mean normalized closed-loop cost by thirteen point two four to thirteen point five nine percentage points. Experimental results confirm that ART of PIV effectively controls flow within physical systems by successfully tracking prescribed flow fields. This work indicates a significant advancement in applying machine learning to enhance the reliability of flow measurement techniques.

items.title: GenDSR: Transferring Representations from Video Generation Models for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: GenDSR transfers representations from video generation models to vision-language models to enable dynamic spatial reasoning. The framework creates two branches from video model features: one for holistic context and one for temporal variation. Task-conditioned tokenwise gates fuse these signals to refine the visual representation. On DSR-Bench, GenDSR achieved 67.2%, setting a new state-of-the-art result.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "GenDSR: Transferring Representations from Video Generation Models for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning" details a framework for transferring representations from video generation models to vision-language models to enable dynamic spatial reasoning, achieving a state-of-the-art result on DSR-Bench with sixty-seven point two percent accuracy. The GenDSR framework establishes two branches derived from video model features, one capturing holistic context and another representing temporal variation. Task-conditioned tokenwise gates are employed to fuse these distinct signals, refining the visual representation through this process. This methodology allows the model to interpret and reason about dynamic spatial relationships present in video data more effectively. The advancement demonstrates a method for leveraging complex temporal data to enhance spatial understanding in artificial intelligence systems. Future research will focus on extending this technique to more complex reasoning tasks.

items.title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
items.summary: Effective image editing evaluation requires identifying local failures to guide subsequent model improvements. WeGenEditBench introduces 2,740 evaluation instances across various editing tasks, incorporating item-level deductions and visual evidence. WeGenEvoStudio is a multi-agent harness designed for recursive self-improvement by integrating failure diagnosis and adaptation. Experiments show that this approach leads to substantial targeted gains in image editing model performance. The work provides a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models" details a framework for improving image editing models through systematic evaluation and iterative self-improvement. The research introduces WeGenEditBench, which comprises two thousand seven hundred forty evaluation instances across various editing tasks, incorporating item-level deductions and visual evidence. Furthermore, WeGenEvoStudio is presented as a multi-agent harness engineered for recursive self-improvement by integrating failure diagnosis and adaptation mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that this integrated approach yields substantial targeted gains in the performance of image editing models. This work establishes a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning processes. The findings indicate a pathway toward more robust and reliably evolving generative models in the field.

items.title: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D
items.summary: Coarse3D generates controllable and faithful sparse 3D structure from arbitrary images for image-to-3D tasks. It addresses limitations in existing coarse generators by controlling orientation and ensuring structural consistency with input images. The method employs a first-frame anchored canonical space, a dual-tower DiT, and spatial-prior guided attention for structure generation. Coarse3D can replace the coarse stage in existing pipelines to produce high-quality sparse structure. Experiments demonstrate that this approach substantially improves structure quality and enhances final 3D generation, achieving state-of-the-art results.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D" details a method for generating controllable and faithful sparse three-dimensional structure from arbitrary images. The research introduces Coarse3D, which addresses limitations in existing coarse generators by controlling orientation and ensuring structural consistency with input images. The method employs a first-frame anchored canonical space, a dual-tower diffusion transformer, and spatial-prior guided attention for structure generation. This approach can replace the coarse stage in existing pipelines to produce high-quality sparse structure. Experiments conducted with this approach demonstrate a substantial improvement in structure quality and an enhancement in final three-dimensional generation, achieving state-of-the-art results in the field. This advancement signals a significant step forward in the fidelity and control of image-to-3D reconstruction tasks.

items.title: Erase the Injected Region: Multimodal Prompt-Injection Defense with On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: Multimodal prompt injection embeds malicious instructions in external media, posing a challenge for existing defenses that often impair task utility. ERASE is an on-policy self-distillation method that defends against this by erasing the injected region and replacing it with modality-appropriate blank content. The method trains a student model by observing feedback from a frozen base model reading the erased view through token-level feedback. Experiments show ERASE achieves near-zero observed attack success while retaining task utility close to the undefended input level. This approach significantly reduces injection dependence, demonstrating improved robustness across different modalities.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Erase the Injected Region: Multimodal Prompt-Injection Defense with On-Policy Self-Distillation" details a method for defending against multimodal prompt injection by erasing injected content and replacing it with appropriate blank material. The research presents an on-policy self-distillation technique called ERASE, which defends against malicious instructions embedded in external media. This method operates by training a student model using feedback from a frozen base model observing the erased view via token-level feedback. Experimental results indicate that ERASE achieves near-zero observed attack success while maintaining task utility close to the level of the undefended input. This approach demonstrates a significant reduction in injection dependence and improved robustness across various modalities. The findings suggest a pathway toward more resilient multimodal systems against sophisticated injection attacks.

items.title: Transferring Peptide-Target Interaction Patterns to Small Molecules by Joint Guidance for Diffusion and Flow Matching
items.summary: Generating small molecules for protein-protein interactions is challenging because PPI interfaces are broad, unlike small-molecule binding pockets. The PIFT framework transfers peptide-target interaction patterns to small molecules using joint guidance of diffusion and flow matching. This method maps peptide and small-molecule interfaces into a shared space to capture transferable interface information across molecular types. The process uses peptide-derived references to steer molecule generation, resulting in improved interface recovery and favorable properties. Experiments confirm that this guidance enhances cross-modal compatibility and docking performance for small molecules.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Transferring Peptide-Target Interaction Patterns to Small Molecules by Joint Guidance for Diffusion and Flow Matching" describes a method for transferring peptide-target interaction patterns to small molecules using joint guidance of diffusion and flow matching, demonstrating improved interface recovery and favorable properties. The PIFT framework achieves this by mapping peptide and small-molecule interfaces into a shared space to capture transferable interface information across molecular types. The process utilizes peptide-derived references to steer the generation of small molecules, which results in enhanced cross-modal compatibility and improved docking performance for the generated small molecules. This research confirms that joint guidance effectively enhances the transfer of interface information between different molecular entities. This development indicates a potential advance in AI-driven small molecule design for biological targets.

items.title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
items.summary: Vision transformer models like CLIP can achieve few-shot defect detection using limited images, but structured decision models like Jev and Clef-Flash offer improvements. The research introduces a framework for k-shot learning, an agentic approach to refine text descriptions, and a calibration method for defect probabilities. Testing across five manufacturing cases showed Jev and Clef-Flash outperformed CLIP's accuracy with fewer references. Agentic text refinement significantly improved accuracy, and calibration reduced the Brier score in many configurations.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models" details a framework for few-shot defect detection utilizing calibrated decision models. The research demonstrated that structured decision models offer improvements over vision transformer models like CLIP in defect detection when using limited images. The study introduced a framework for k-shot learning involving an agentic approach to refine text descriptions and a calibration method for defect probabilities. Testing across five manufacturing cases indicated that the Jev and Clef-Flash models outperformed CLIP's accuracy with fewer references, and agentic text refinement significantly improved overall accuracy. Furthermore, calibration successfully reduced the Brier score across many configurations. This work suggests that incorporating structured decision models and calibration techniques enhances the performance of few-shot visual inspection systems.
